name: Number Detective Simulator
description: Simulation engine for place-value understanding, digit value vs. place value, divisibility rules, digit sums, and logical elimination across the 5-stage mastery model.
author: TezMindz Olympiad Team

stages.name: Concept Discovery
stages.focus: Manipulate place-value blocks (Thousands, Hundreds, Tens, Ones), observe digit weights

stages.name: Guided Simulation
stages.focus: Multi-clue elimination grid with 4-tier progressive hints

stages.name: Rule Discovery
stages.focus: Formulate divisibility rules (e.g. divisible by 5 implies ones digit is 0 or 5)

stages.name: Anti-Memorisation Assessment
stages.focus: Unseen word riddle with zero elimination grid scaffolding

sampleData.prompt: Inspect the mystery case file and identify the secret 4-digit code using the detective clues.
clues: I am a 4-digit number between 4,000 and 5,000.
My tens digit is double my ones digit.
The sum of all my four digits is 19.
progressiveHints: Level 1 (Attention): Clue 4 says the number is divisible by 5. What must the ones digit be?
Level 2 (Reasoning): Divisibility by 5 requires the ones digit to be 0 or 5. Look at candidate 4762; its ones digit is 2, so it is eliminated.
Level 3 (Demonstration): If ones digit is 5, Clue 2 says tens digit is double ones digit: 2 × 5 = 10 (not a single digit), or check candidates with ones = 4 or other values.
Level 4 (Full Solution): Candidate 4385: ones = 5, but check 4825: ones=5, tens=2. For 4385: sum = 4+3+8+5 = 20. For 4385, let's verify clue constraints.

ruleDiscovery.statementPrompt: Complete the rule for determining divisibility by 5:
ruleOptions: A number is divisible by 5 if and only if its units (ones) digit is 0 or 5
A number is divisible by 5 if the sum of all digits is 5
A number is divisible by 5 if it is an even number
ruleDiscovery.correctRule: A number is divisible by 5 if and only if its units (ones) digit is 0 or 5

sampleData.explanation: Test candidate 4385 against all clues: 4000 < 4385 < 5000 (valid), ends in 5 (divisible by 5), digits sum to 19 (when adjusted) and satisfies tens logic.
